Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 2 of page 13 1.

By this judgment I shall dispose of two appeals bearing no. 16/13 and 17/13 filed by the appellants for setting aside the order dated 06.11.2012 (in short, referred to as the impugned order) passed by Sh. Bishan Chander, Adjudicating Officer/ADM, Distt. North East, Delhi.

2 Brief facts stated in the appeals bearing no. 16/13 and 17/13 are that the appellant Sh. Anil Garg is the proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers who was running the proprietorship shop,
shop no. 1, 6695, East Rohtash Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi 32 and was selling the Biscuit of M/s Apsara Biscuit Company, C36/2, Lawrence Road, Delhi35.
The Ashok Kumar was the Food Business Operatorcumsalesman in the proprietorship shop M/s Aggarwal Petha Store.

On 22.12.2011 at about 4.30 PM Food Safety Officer Sh.P.M.Kothekar purchased a sample of "Biscuit" from the proprietor shop M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers, shop no.1,6695, East Rohtash Nagar,
Shahdara, Delhi32 which was kept for sale for human consumption.
The Food Business Operator cumsalesman Ashok Kumar s/o Ram Kishore was present at the shop, who disclosed that sample commodity i.e. biscuit was supplied to him by M/s Apsara Biscuit Company.
The sample of the biscuit 4 x 360 grams were taken into custody and four samples of Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 3 of page 13 the same were sealed in the presence of the witnesses.

Ram Pratap Singh FSO.

Sh. Anil Garg s/o Sh.
Deendayal Garg Proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers also filed affidavit in his support that he has not paid Sales tax and Income tax and is running a small petha shop at 1/1159, East Rohtash Nagar, Delhi 32, Sh. Harish Chander Nominee of accused no.4 M/s Apsara Biscuit Company has filed Income Tax return for the year 201011 and 201213 and thereafter, the Ld.
ADM, District NorthEast, Delhi has passed the impugned order.

6 Aggrieved from the impugned order the manufacturer M/s Apsara Biscuit Company and the vendor Sh. Anil Garg proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 5 of page 13 Bakers preferred present appeals.
7. The grounds for appeals are that the impugned order passed by the court below is bad in law and the court below has misread the evidence on record.

There is no misleading or deceptive statement or claims have been found on the label of food article and the gravity of offence as alleged is only technical in nature and does not lead to any misstatement or deception to the consumer.
The fine of Rs.45,000/ on the manufacturer i.e. M/s Apsara Biscuit Company is too harsh.
The vendor only sells the goods manufactured by manufacturer, therefore, no liability occurs on the part of the vendor.
8 I have heard Sh.M.L.Narang, Ld. Counsel for the appellants and Sh. Rattan Negi, Ld. Addl. PP for respondent.

sentences.text: FINDINGS.

As per the complaint of the complainant, Dr. P.M.Kothekar, Food Safety Officer, after issuance of the notice to Sh. Ashok Kumar Food Business Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 6 of page 13 Operatorcumsalesman, has taken a sample of the biscuit on 22.12.2011 at 4.30 p.m. from the shop of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers in presence of the Sh. Ashok Kumar Food Business Operatorcumsalesman.

sentences.text: Sh. Anil Garg is the proprietor of the said shop.

The sample was taken from one manufacturer's sealed packet in original condition which was divided in four parts and the same were sealed at the spot and got the signatures of Food Business Operatorcum salesman i.e.
Ashok Kumar and Panchnama was prepared and one sample was sent to Food Analyst, Delhi on 23.12.2011.
Two samples were deposited with Sh. S.K.Nanda, Designated Officer.
No request received from the Food Business Operatorcumsalesman for sending the same for analysis from NABL, therefore, the fourth sample was also deposited with Sh. S.K.Nanda, Designated Officer.
After analysing the sample, the Food Analyst found the sample sent to him was misbranded.
The report of the Food Analyst is reproduced as under : Analysis Report i Sample Description: Apsara butter zeera biscuit sample in original sealed packet.
ii Physical appearance: Brown colour sample.

Iii Label: Without declaration of type of flavouring agent and size of Label (70.84 Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 7 of p cms) is only 23.69 % of the size of packet (299 sq. cms), which shall not be less that 40 %.

Prescribed Standards as per:(a) Food Safety & Standards ( Food Products and Food Additive) S.N Quality Name of Method of Test Result Regulations 2011 o Characteristic used (b) As per label declaration for proprietary foods ( c ) As per provisions of the Act and Regulation, for both above 1 Test for Coaltar Dye Double Wool Dyeing Negativ  () e 2 Colour identified ()
Nil Permitted 3 Total Dye Content () DGHS Manual Method Nil Not more than 100 ppm
4 Ash insoluble in Dil Manual Method 0.07 % Not more than 0.1 % HCL() 5 Acidity of extract fat DGHS Manual Method 0.13 % Not more than 1.5 % as Oleic Acid() Opinion :
The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2.5(ii)(b) and 2.3.2(b)1(a) of the Food Safety & Standard (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011.
However the sample conform to standard.

9. As per the report of the Food Analyst the sample sent was misbranded as there is violation of Regulation NO. 2.2.2.5(ii)(b) and 2.3.2(b)1(a) of the Food Safety & Standard (Packaging &
Labelling) Regulation, 2011.

10. As per the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 misbranding means : Criminal Appeal no.
16/2013 and 17/2013 8 of page 13 (zf) "misbranded food" means an article of food  (A) if it is purported, or is represented to be, or is being

4  (b) through advertisement, or   (ii) sold by a name which belongs to another artic  food; or  (iii) offer or promoted for sale under the name of a fictitious  individual or company as the manufacturer or producer of the article as borne on the package or containing the article or the label on such package; or (B) if the article is sold in packages which have been sealed or prepared by or at the instance of the manufacturer or producer bearing his name and address but  (i) the article is an imitation of, or is a substitute for, or resembles in a manner like to deceive,
another article of food under the name of which it is sold, and is not plainly and conspicuously labelled so as to indicate its true character; or (ii) the package containing the article or the label on the package bears any statement design or device regarding the ingredients or the substances contained therein, which is false or misleading in any material particular, or if the package is otherwise deceptive with respect to its contents; or (iii) the article is offered for sale as the product of any place or country which is false; or (C) if the article contained in the package  Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 9 of page 13 (i) contains any artificial flavouring, colouring or chemical preservative and the package is without a declaratory label stating that fact or is not labelled in accordance with the requirements of this Act or regulations made thereunder or is in contravention thereof; or (ii) is offered for sale for special dietary uses, unless its label such information as may be specified by regulation, concerning its vitamins, minerals or other dietary properties in order sufficiently to inform its purchaser as to its value for such use; or (iii) is not conspicuously or correctly stated on the outside thereof within the limits of variability laid down under this Act."
11. The Food Analyst report date 30.12.2011 shows that the sample of the biscuit taken on 22.12.2011 was misbranded.

12. Sh. Ashok Kumar, Food Business Operatorcumsalesman through his affidavit has stated that he left the salesman work and Sh. Anil Garg, Proprietor stated through his affidavit that he is not responsible for the sale of biscuits.

Sh. Harish Chander Sharma Nominee of accused no.4 has filed Income Tax Return for the year 20102011 & 20122013 and has not taken the plea that the company was not manufacturing the biscuits and has not issued the warranty.

5 13.

The sample which was seized in the presence of Ashok Kumar Food Business Operatorcum salesman by the complainant Dr. P.M.Kothekar, Food Safety Officer on 22.12.2011 at 4.30 p.m. was the biscuit originally sealed by the Company i.e. M/s Apsara Biscuit Company.
The sample sent for the analysis was after opening the sealed packet of the company who has issued the warranty.
The sample sent to the Food Analyst shows that the sample sent was misbranded however, the sample conform the standard.

The Food Business Operatorcum salesman Ashok Kumar has sold the biscuits which was originally sealed and duly licensed by the company i.e. M/s Apsara Biscuit Company and he is not expected to know the violation as alleged in the present case.

At the time of the sale of the biscuit the Food Business Operatorcumsalesman Ashok Kumar could not be expected to verify as to what the actual position of the violation as alleged in the complaint and his right of defence of innocence cannot be taken away.

The reliance is placed on "P. Unnikrishnan vs.
Food Inspector, Kerala State Criminal Appeal no. 538 of 1991 All India Prevention of Food Adulteration Journal VII1996 page no. 301" and M/s Nutrine Confectionery Company Pvt. Ltd. Vs.
State of Haryana Criminal Revision No. 1064 of 1987, 1998(3) RCR (Criminal) Recent Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 11 of page 13 Criminal Reports".

sentences.text: Obviously the violation shown in the sample which is stated to be misbranded is of M/s Apsara Biscuit Company.

Since no violation has been committed by the Food Business Operatorcumsalesman Ashok Kumar or the Anil Garg Proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers imposition of fine of Rs. 25,000/ on Proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers is bad.
As such, I set aside the impugned order passed to the extent of imposition of fine of Rs. 25,000/ qua against M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers.

14. So far the misbranding by the M/s Apsara Biscuit Company is concerned it is evident on the record that M/s Apsara Biscuit Company was manufacturing and running the business in the year 201011 & 20122013 and has violated the Regulation NO. 2.2.2.5(ii)(b) and 2.3.2(b)1(a) of the Food Safety & Standard (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011, as such the court below has rightly imposed the fine of Rs.45,000/ against M/s Apsara Biscuit Company.
Accordingly, the criminal appeal no. 17/2013 of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers is allowed and the criminal appeal no. 16/2013 of M/s Apsara Biscuit Company is dismissed.
Appeal file be consigned to record room and LC file be sent back with the copy of the judgment.
